# robintrmbtt/otlesmix
**Stars**: 0 | **Language**: Jupyter Notebook
**Description**: The OTLesMix repository provides a PyTorch implementation for generating synthetic lesions with diverse shapes and locations using Wasserstein barycenter and optimal transport maps. It includes code for reproducing experimental results, installation instructions for dependencies like PyKeOps and uv, and guidance on data preparation for datasets such as BraTS 2020, ATLAS v2.0, and ISLES 2022. The repository also features example notebooks for synthetic lesion generation.

## README.md
```
# OTLesMix: Wasserstein Barycenter and Optimal Transport Map for Synthetic Lesion Generation with Diverse Shapes and Locations

This repo is the official Pytorch implementation of the article *OTLesMix: Wasserstein Barycenter and Optimal Transport Map for Synthetic Lesion Generation with Diverse Shapes and Locations* (submitted at MICCAI 2026 Workshop SASHIMI)

![Method Overview](images/illustration.png)


## Examples of synthetic lesion generation

We provide in the Jupyter Notebook `notebooks/example.ipynb` a simplified example. It contains all the code required to produce the figure below (Figure 2 in the article). The images used from BraTS 2020 dataset are included in the folder `notebooks/data` and for ATLAS v2.0 and ISLES 2022, you will need to follow the instructions of section [Data preparation](#data-preparation).

![Method Overview](images/examples.png)

## Installation

OTLesMix uses [PyKeOps](https://github.com/getkeops/keops) as main library for Optimal Transport functions. Its installation is a little tricker than usual Python libraries. In particular, it requires a properly configuration, includind a C++ compiler and Cuda Toolkit. If you already have them configured, you can skip the command below and directly go to the installation of the Python packages with `uv`. Another way to do it is with a conda environment, using the command lines provided below (you may need to change the Cuda version). For more detail, please refer to the [installation guide](https://www.kernel-operations.io/keops/python/installation.html) of the library, and make sure your installation is correct with their section called "Testing your implementation".

```
conda create -n otlesmix python=3.12
conda activate otlesmix
pip3 install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126
conda install -c nvidia cuda-toolkit
```

Aside from the C++ compiler installation and Cuda Toolkit, we use `uv` for easier installation of the project and better reproductibility. To install it, use the following command (on Linux and macOS), or have a look at the [official repo](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv).

```
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

Once the installation is done, you can clone this repo and synchronize the project with:

```
git clone [repo] # note: hidden for review
cd otlesmix
uv sync
```

If needed, you can change the environment variable for the nnUNet data folders and the result folder, which set in the file `.env`. Their default values are:

```
nnUNet_raw="datasets/nnUNet_raw"
nnUNet_preprocessed="datasets/nnUNet_preprocessed"
nnUNet_results="results"
```

## Data preparation

In our experiments, we use the datasets BraTS2020, ATLAS v2.0 and ISLES. The first is openly accessible, the two other require access approval. We describe hereunder how to access, download and pre-process the data if you want to reproduce our experiments.

<details>
  <summary>BraTS 2020</summary>

  No extra software is needed to preprocess BraTS 2020.

  To download the dataset, please go the the [Kaggle page of the dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/awsaf49/brats20-dataset-training-validation), or use the following command line:

  ```
  curl -L -o datasets/brats20-dataset-training-validation.zip\
  https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/download/awsaf49/brats20-dataset-training-validation
  ```

  You then need to uncompress the folder:

  ```
  unzip datasets/brats20-dataset-training-validation.zip -d datasets/
  ```

  Finally, you can preprocess the data using the command:
  ```
  uv run --env-file=.env otlesmix/data/brats.py datasets/BraTS2020_TrainingData/MICCAI_BraTS2020_TrainingData
  ```
</details>

<details>
  <summary>ATLAS v2.0</summary>
  
  To preprocess the datasets ATLAS v2.0, you will need [Freesurfer](https://surfer.nmr.mgh.harvard.edu/fswiki) with version >= 7.3.2 and [ANTs](https://github.com/antsx/ants). Please refer to their respective installation guides.

  To access the data, you need to register to the [ATLAS R2.0 Grand Challenge](https://atlas.grand-challenge.org/) and follow the instructions given in the section Dataset. After downloading and extracting the data, you can run the preprocessing script with:

  ```
  uv run --env-file=.env otlesmix/data/atlas.py /path/to/ATLAS_2
  ```
</details>

<details>
  <summary>ISLES 2022</summary>

  To preprocess the datasets ISLES 2022, you will need [Freesurfer](https://surfer.nmr.mgh.harvard.edu/fswiki) with version >= 7.3.2 and [ANTs](https://github.com/antsx/ants). Please refer to their respective installation guides. You also need the MNI-152 atlas with a 2mm resolution, provided in `notebooks/data/MNI152_T1_2mm_brain.nii.gz`.

  To access the data, you need to register to the [ISLES 2022 Grand Challenge](https://isles22.grand-challenge.org/home/) and follow the instructions given in the section Dataset. After downloading and extracting the data, you can run the preprocessing script with:

  ```
  uv run --env-file=.env otlesmix/data/isles.py /path/to/ISLES-2022 notebooks/data/MNI152_T1_2mm_brain.nii.gz
  ```
</details>

If you have not changed the default parameters of the script, you should obtain in the end three folders in the format of nnUNet datasets named `Dataset100_BraTS`, `Dataset200_ATLAS`, and `Dataset300_ISLES`, and located in the folder `datasets`.

## Usage


### Generate synthetic data

The script to generate synthetic dataset with OTLesMix (or implemented baselines) is `otlesmix/generate_lesion.py` and it uses `hydra` for configuration.

```
uv run --env-file=.env otlesmix/generate_lesion.py +dataset_name=Dataset101_BraTS_OTLesMix lesion_generator=otlesmix data=brats
```

The script requires to have at least `+dataset_name=DatasetXXX_YYY` as argument, which is the name that will be given to the synthetic dataset (it must satifies the nomemclature of nnUNet). 

The two other main arguments are `lesion_generator=XXX`, which can take the values `otlesmix`, `carvemix`, `cutmix` or `mixup`, and  `data=XXX`, whose accepted values are `brats`, `atlas` and `isles`.

Additionally, you can modify other parameters, such as the number of generated samples with `brats/n_synthles=XXX`

### Training, inference and evaluation

Once the augmented datasets have been generated, we can use nnUNet to train and evaluate the segmentation models. The main commands to use are given below. If you have any trouble, please refer to the [documentation of nnUNet](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet). If the commands from nnUNet does not work properly with `uv`, you can also use a standalone installation of nnUNet and manually specify the associated paths (e.g. `nnUNet_raw=XXX'`)

```
# planning and preprocessing
uv run --env-file=.env nnUNetv2_plan_and_preprocess -d 101 --verifiy_dataset_integrity

# training
uv run --env-file=.env nnUNetv2_train 101 2d 0 -tr nnUNetTrainer_500epochs

#inference
uv run --env-file=.env nnUNetv2_predict -i datasets/nnunet_raw/Dataset100_BraTS/imagesTs/ -o results/Dataset101_BraTS_OTLesMix/nnUNetTrainer_500epochs__nnUNetPlans__3d_fullres/fold_0/inference -d 101 -tr nnUNetTrainer_500epochs -c 2d -f 0 --save_probabilities
```

Note that depending on the experiment you want to reproduce and your configuration (paths, dataset names, etc.), you may need to change some of the parameters of the commands above. For instance, on ATLAS v2.0 and ISLES 2022, you should use the configuration `3d_fullres`.

Finally, you can evaluate the model on the test set with:

```
uv run --env-file=.env otlesmix/eval/evaluation.py --pred_paths datasets/nnunet_raw/Dataset100_BraTS/imagesTs/ --gt_path datasets/nnunet_raw/Dataset100_BraTS/labelsTs/ --brats
```

Giving multiple paths to `--pred_paths` will run statistical comparisons between the provided result folders.

## Results

| Method | BraTS (WT) | BraTS (TC) | BraTS (ET) | ATLAS | ISLES |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TDA | 77.0 ± 30.1*** | 72.5 ± 29.6*** | 66.4 ± 30.9*** | 45.8 ± 33.8*** | 68.8 ± 22.4*** |
| MixUp | 80.6 ± 24.5*** | 75.2 ± 24.7*** | 68.2 ± 27.6*** | 43.7 ± 33.0*** | 66.3 ± 23.9*** |
| CutMix | 81.9 ± 22.5*** | 76.7 ± 23.1*** | 70.0 ± 26.7*** | 48.1 ± 33.2** | 69.8 ± 22.6*** |
| CarveMix | 82.5 ± 22.3*** | 77.2 ± 23.1*** | 69.6 ± 26.9*** | 48.5 ± 32.5* | 70.8 ± 21.4** |
| OTLesMix | **83.3 ± 22.8** | **78.4 ± 23.2** | **71.4 ± 26.5** | **49.9 ± 32.9** | **71.7 ± 20.8** |

> Average and standard deviation of the DSC (%) on the three test datasets. The best model on each task is highlighted in bold. Asterisks indicate the level of statistical significance of the difference in DSC between a given method and the best performing one with a pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank test (\*: p ≤ 0.05, \*\*: p ≤ 0.01, \*\*\*: p ≤ 0.001).
```

## otlesmix/data/brats.py

```
import os
from argparse import ArgumentParser
import nibabel as nib
import numpy as np
from tqdm import tqdm
import torch
import json
from scipy.ndimage import binary_dilation
from skimage.measure import label

import rootutils
rootutils.setup_root(__file__, indicator=".project-root", pythonpath=True)

from otlesmix.data.base_dataset import BaseDataset
from otlesmix.data.utils import normalize_img

class BraTSDataset(BaseDataset):
    def get_restrict_mask(self, patid):
        list_images = sorted([f for f in os.listdir(os.path.join(self.data_path, 'imagesTr')) 
                        if f.startswith(patid) and f.endswith('.nii.gz')])
        img = nib.load(os.path.join(self.data_path, 'imagesTr', list_images[0])).get_fdata()

        brainmask = (img == 0)
        labeled_mask, n_labels = label(brainmask, connectivity=2, return_num=True)
        largest_label = 1 + np.argmax([np.sum(labeled_mask == i) for i in range(1, n_labels + 1)])
        brainmask = 1 - (labeled_mask == largest_label)
        return brainmask

if __name__ == '__main__':
    aparser = ArgumentParser()
    aparser.add_argument('data_path', type=str, help='Path to BraTS dataset')
    aparser.add_argument('--save_path', type=str, default=None, help='Path to save extracted slices')
```

```
import numpy as np
import nibabel as nib

def normalize_img(img):
    p_1, p_99 = np.percentile(img[img > 0], (1, 99))
    img[img > 0] = np.clip(img[img > 0], p_1, p_99)
    img[img > 0] = (img[img > 0] - p_1) / (p_99 - p_1)
    return img

def restrict_to_central_slices(path, min_max=[50, 110], is_mask=False):
    nii = nib.load(path)
    data = nii.get_fdata()[..., min_max[0]:min_max[1]]
    if is_mask:
        data = np.rint(data).astype(np.uint8)
    new_nii = nib.Nifti1Image(
        data, affine=nii.affine, header=nii.header
    )
    nib.save(new_nii, path)
```

```
import numpy as np
import nibabel as nib

def compute_dice(pred, gt, eps=1e-6):
    pred = pred.astype(bool)
    gt = gt.astype(bool)

    intersection = np.sum(pred & gt)
    union = np.sum(pred) + np.sum(gt)

    dice_score = (2. * intersection + eps) / (union + eps)
    return dice_score

def compute_metrics_brats(pred, target):
    results = {}
    # whole tumor
    mask_gt = (target != 0).astype(int)
    mask_pred = (pred != 0).astype(int)
    results['dice_WT'] = compute_dice(mask_gt, mask_pred)
    del mask_gt, mask_pred

    # tumor core
    mask_gt = ((target == 1) | (target == 2)).astype(int)
    mask_pred = ((pred == 1) | (pred == 2)).astype(int)
    results['dice_TC'] = compute_dice(mask_gt, mask_pred)
    del mask_gt, mask_pred

    # enhancing
    mask_gt = (target == 2).astype(int)
    mask_pred = (pred == 2).astype(int)
    results['dice_ET'] = compute_dice(mask_gt, mask_pred)
    del mask_gt, mask_pred

    return results
```

```
import os

import numpy as np
from tqdm import tqdm
from argparse import ArgumentParser
import nibabel as nib
import scipy.stats

import rootutils
rootutils.setup_root(__file__, indicator=".project-root", pythonpath=True)

from otlesmix.eval.utils import compute_dice, compute_metrics_brats

if __name__ == '__main__':
    aparser = ArgumentParser()
    aparser.add_argument('--pred_paths', nargs='+', type=str, help='Path to folder(s) containing predicted segmentation files')
    aparser.add_argument('--gt_path', required=True, type=str, help='Path to ground truth file')
    aparser.add_argument('--brats', action='store_true', help='Whether to compute BraTS-specific metrics (WT, TC, ET)')
    aparser.add_argument('--output_path_stat_tests', type=str, default=None, help='Path to save the results of statistical tests (.txt). If not provided, the results will only be printed.')
    args = aparser.parse_args()

    full_results = {}

    for pred_path in tqdm(args.pred_paths, desc="Processing prediction folders", leave=True):

        pred_list = sorted([f.split('.')[0] for f in os.listdir(pred_path) if f.endswith('.nii.gz')])

        results = {}

        for patid in tqdm(pred_list, desc="Computing metrics", leave=False):
            pred_file = os.path.join(pred_path, f'{patid}.nii.gz')
            gt_file = os.path.join(args.gt_path, f'{patid}.nii.gz')
            assert os.path.exists(gt_file), f'Ground truth file for patient {patid} not found at {gt_file}'

            nii_pred = nib.load(pred_file)
            nii_gt = nib.load(gt_file)

            spacing = np.abs(nii_pred.affine[:nii_pred.ndim, :nii_pred.ndim].diagonal())
            if args.brats:
                metrics = compute_metrics_brats(nii_pred.get_fdata(), nii_gt.get_fdata())
            else:
                metrics = {}
                metrics['dice'] = compute_dice(nii_pred.get_fdata(), nii_gt.get_fdata())
            for key in metrics.keys():
                results[patid] = {
                    key: metrics[key] for key in metrics.keys()
                }

        results['AVG'] = {metric: np.mean([res[metric] for res in results.values()]) for metric in metrics.keys()}
        results['STD'] = {metric: np.std([res[metric] for res in results.values()]) for metric in metrics.keys()}
        print('Average Dice Scores:')
        for metric in results['AVG'].keys():
            print(f'{metric}: {results["AVG"][metric]:.4f} +/- {results["STD"][metric]:.4f}')

        with open(os.path.join(pred_path, 'metrics.json'), 'w') as f:
            json.dump(results, f, indent=4, ensure_ascii=False)

        results['pred_path'] = pred_path
        full_results[pred_path] = results

    if len(full_results) <= 1:
        print("Only one prediction folder provided, skipping statistical tests.")
    else:
        # check that all results have the same set of patients
        patient_sets = [set(res.keys()) for res in full_results.values()]
        if not all(patient_set == patient_sets[0] for patient_set in patient_sets):
            raise ValueError("All prediction folders must have results for the same set of patients to perform statistical tests.")
        patient_sets = patient_sets[0] - {'AVG', 'STD', 'pred_path'}

        for metric in set(metric for metric in full_results[list(full_results.keys())[0]]['AVG'].keys()):
            print(f"\nStatistical tests for metric: {metric}")
            best = max(full_results.values(), key=lambda x: x['AVG'][metric])
            # Perform pairwise wilcoxon signed-rank tests between the best method and all others
            for pred_path, res in full_results.items():
                if pred_path == best['pred_path']:
                    continue
                stat, p_value = scipy.stats.wilcoxon(
                    [best[patid][metric] for patid in patient_sets],
                    [res[patid][metric] for patid in patient_sets],
                    alternative='greater',
                    correction=False
                )
                print(f"Comparing {best['pred_path']} vs {pred_path}: p-value = {p_value:.4e}")
                if args.output_path_stat_tests is not None:
                    if args.output_path_stat_tests.endswith('.txt'):
                        with open(args.output_path_stat_tests, 'a') as f:
                            f.write(f"{best['pred_path']} vs {pred_path} for metric {metric}: p-value = {p_value:.4e}\n")
                    else:
                        raise ValueError("Output path for statistical tests must end with .txt")
```
